Results.Description: The name that identifies this computer on the network. Helpdesk uses it to find the right machine in the inventory and in remote support tools.
The Windows edition, feature release and build. It decides which features and security updates the computer can receive.
Whether Microsoft still releases security updates for this Windows version. A version that is out of support stays vulnerable to every newly found security hole.
Results.Recommendation: Support for this Windows version ends soon. Install the newest feature update: Settings > Windows Update.

Results.Description: The date this Windows installation was set up. An old installation tends to collect leftover software and settings.
Who made the computer and which model it is. Needed to find drivers, spare parts and warranty information.
Whether the computer is managed centrally in a company domain or stands alone in a workgroup. It decides where user accounts and policies come from.
The account that is using the computer right now. Problems are often tied to one user profile rather than to the whole machine.
The time zone the clock is set to. A wrong time zone shifts meeting times and can make sign-in to online services fail.
The time since Windows was last started. A restart clears the memory, finishes updates and resets drivers, so a long uptime is a common cause of slowness.
Results.Recommendation: Restart the computer; it has been running for more than 7 days. Use Restart, not Shut down: with Fast Startup enabled a shutdown does not reset the uptime.

Results.Description: The score Windows itself keeps in Reliability Monitor, from 1 (unstable) to 10 (stable). It drops after crashes, hangs and failed installations and recovers while the computer runs without problems.
Activation confirms that this copy of Windows has a valid license. Without it Windows shows reminders and locks the personalization settings.
Programs that start automatically when the user signs in. Each one makes sign-in slower and keeps using memory in the background.
Results.Value: 12 programs: Chat Client, Cloud Backup, Contoso Updater, Contoso VPN, Mail Notifier, OneDrive, PDF Helper, Printer Assistant and 4 more

Results.Description: How long Windows needed to start the last time it measured it, from power-on until the desktop was usable. A slow startup is usually caused by too many startup programs or a slow disk.
Results.Recommendation: Windows only shows this to administrators. Start the tool as administrator to include it: in the window use "Restart as administrator", in a console open PowerShell with "Run as administrator".

Results.Description: The folders under C:\Users where each user keeps documents, downloads and program settings, and how much space each one takes.
Results.Recommendation: Windows only shows this to administrators. Start the tool as administrator to include it: in the window use "Restart as administrator", in a console open PowerShell with "Run as administrator".

Results.Description: The processor (CPU) executes every program. More cores and a higher clock speed let the computer do more work at the same time.
RAM is the short-term working memory of running programs. The module layout and the free slots show whether more memory can be added.
Results.Value: 16 GB (2 x 8 GB DDR4, 3200 MHz), 2 of 2 slots used

Results.Description: The graphics adapter draws everything shown on the screen. The driver version matters when the picture flickers or video and games misbehave.
A monitor connected to the computer: its model, manufacturer code and year of manufacture.
The main board that all other components plug into. Its model decides which processors, memory and expansion cards are supported.
The firmware that starts the hardware before Windows loads. An outdated version can cause compatibility and stability problems.
The unique number the manufacturer gave this computer. It is used for warranty claims and asset tracking.
How busy the processor was while the check ran. Constantly high load makes the whole computer slow and the fans loud.
How much of the installed RAM is in use. When it is nearly full, Windows moves data to the much slower disk and everything starts to lag.
Results.Recommendation: Memory is almost full. Close unused applications and browser tabs; if this happens regularly, the computer needs more RAM.

Results.Description: The programs that hold the most RAM right now. This is the first place to look when memory usage is high.
Results.Value: msedge (4.9 GB), Teams (2.1 GB), EXCEL (1.6 GB), OUTLOOK (1.2 GB), Memory Compression (0.9 GB)

Results.Description: A physical SSD or hard disk and the health state it reports about itself. A drive that reports problems can fail and take the data with it.
A physical SSD or hard disk and the health state it reports about itself. A drive that reports problems can fail and take the data with it.
Results.Recommendation: The drive reports a problem and may fail. Back up the data now and plan to replace the drive.

Results.Description: A drive letter (partition) and its free space. Windows needs free space for updates, temporary files and virtual memory.
Results.Recommendation: The disk is almost full. Free up space now: Windows updates and applications can fail without free space.

Results.Description: A drive letter (partition) and its free space. Windows needs free space for updates, temporary files and virtual memory.
Files that programs left in the temporary folder of the user. They are safe to remove and often the quickest way to free space on a full disk.
Results.Recommendation: Temporary files take up a lot of space. Remove them in Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files.

Results.Description: Everything the user has downloaded and never moved or deleted. Old installers and duplicates here are a common reason for a full disk.
Deleted files still take up disk space until the Recycle Bin is emptied.
A file on the disk that Windows uses as extra memory when the RAM is full. Heavy use means the computer is short of memory and slow.
What a drive measures about itself (SMART): its temperature, how much of its rated lifetime is used up, how long it has been powered on and how many read or write errors it could not correct.
Results.Recommendation: Windows only shows this to administrators. Start the tool as administrator to include it: in the window use "Restart as administrator", in a console open PowerShell with "Run as administrator".

Results.Description: Whether Windows has flagged a drive as possibly damaged and in need of a disk check. A drive is flagged after a crash or power loss while data was being written.
Results.Recommendation: Windows only shows this to administrators. Start the tool as administrator to include it: in the window use "Restart as administrator", in a console open PowerShell with "Run as administrator".

Results.Description: Temporary files that Windows and installers leave in C:\Windows\Temp. They are safe to remove with Disk Cleanup.
Results.Recommendation: Windows only shows this to administrators. Start the tool as administrator to include it: in the window use "Restart as administrator", in a console open PowerShell with "Run as administrator".

Results.Description: Hardware that Windows found but cannot use, shown with a yellow mark in Device Manager. Usually the driver is missing or failed to start.
The charge of the laptop battery and whether the charger is connected.
The programs listed under Installed apps in Settings. Useful to see what is on the computer and which versions.
Results.Value: 12 programs: 7-Zip 24.08, Chat Client 5.2, Contoso Office 16.0, Contoso VPN 3.1, Mail Client 12.4, PDF Reader 2025.1, Printer Assistant 2.0, Screenshot Tool 4.0 and 4 more

Results.Description: Programs installed in the last weeks. When a problem is new, something installed recently is a likely cause.
Results.Value: 2 in the last 30 days: Screenshot Tool (2026-09-22), PDF Reader (2026-09-11)

Results.Description: How often programs stopped working unexpectedly, and which ones. A program that crashes again and again needs an update or a reinstall.
Results.Value: 9 in the last 7 days: EXCEL.EXE (6), msedge.exe (2), Teams.exe (1)
Results.Recommendation: Programs crash more often than usual. Update or reinstall the program at the top of the list; the details of each crash are in Event Viewer (eventvwr.msc) > Windows Logs > Application, source "Application Error".

Results.Description: The browser that opens when a link is clicked in e-mail or another program.
How often the computer went off without a proper shutdown (power loss, crash, forced power-off). It risks data loss and points to power or stability problems.
Results.Recommendation: The computer lost power or crashed without shutting down properly. Check the power cable or battery, overheating and recently installed drivers.

Results.Description: How often Windows itself crashed and showed the blue stop screen. It points to a faulty driver or failing hardware.
Errors and warnings logged by the disk drivers and the file system, such as bad blocks and failed writes. They are an early sign of a failing drive or cable.
Results.Recommendation: The disk or the file system reported problems. Back up important data, check the drive health in the Hardware category and run "chkdsk /scan" as administrator. Repeated errors usually mean the drive or its cable is failing.

Results.Description: Errors that the hardware itself reported to Windows (WHEA), for example a faulty memory module or an overheating processor.
The most severe events recorded by Windows itself and its drivers, such as crashes and sudden power loss.
Results.Recommendation: Critical events usually mean crashes or unexpected shutdowns. Open Event Viewer (eventvwr.msc) > Windows Logs > System and filter by level Critical.

Results.Description: Errors recorded by Windows components, drivers and services. A few are normal; many from one source point to a recurring problem.
The components that logged the most errors. They show where to start looking in Event Viewer.
Results.Value: Service Control Manager (14), Microsoft-Windows-DistributedCOM (11), disk (4), Microsoft-Windows-Kernel-Power (2), Netwtw14 (2)

Results.Description: The most severe events recorded by installed programs.
Errors recorded by installed programs, for example crashes and hangs.
The programs that logged the most errors. They show which application is causing trouble.
The most recent Windows update on this computer. Updates close security holes, so a long gap leaves the computer exposed.
Whether Windows is waiting for a restart to finish installing updates. Until then the updates are not fully applied.
Results.Recommendation: Restart the computer to finish installing updates.

Results.Description: Whether Windows Update was paused in Settings. While it is paused no security updates are installed.
The part of Microsoft Defender Antivirus that scans files and programs the moment they are opened. Without it malware is not stopped in time.
The list of known threats the antivirus uses to recognize malware. It has to be updated often to catch new threats.
A Defender setting that stops programs, including malware, from switching the antivirus off or changing its settings.
When Microsoft Defender last scanned the computer for malware that is already on it. Real-time protection only checks files as they are opened.
Malware and unwanted programs that Microsoft Defender has found on this computer, and whether any of them is still active.
The firewall rules used while the computer is connected to the company domain network. The firewall blocks unwanted incoming connections.
The firewall rules used on networks marked as private, such as a home or small office network.
The firewall rules used on public networks such as cafes and airports, where the protection matters most.
Results.Recommendation: Turn on Windows Defender Firewall for this profile (Windows Security > Firewall & network protection), unless a third-party firewall is installed.

Results.Description: UAC asks for confirmation before a program can make changes to Windows. It stops programs from silently taking administrator rights.
A Windows feature that lets someone sign in to this computer from another one. Handy for support, but an open door if it is not needed.
Whether the signed-in user is a standard user or a local administrator. An administrator account can change anything on the computer.
The accounts in the local Administrators group. Each of them has full control over the computer, so the list should be short.
A Windows setting that signs a user in at startup without asking for a password. Anyone who switches the computer on gets into that account.
The user accounts that exist on this computer itself (not in a company domain) and can sign in.
A built-in account without a password, meant for visitors. Left enabled, it lets anyone use the computer.
The administrator account every Windows installation has. It is disabled by default because it is a well-known target for attacks.
Folders on this computer that other computers on the network can open.
A UEFI feature that lets only trusted, signed software start the computer. It protects against malware that loads before Windows.
A security chip that stores encryption keys safely. BitLocker and Windows Hello rely on it, and Windows 11 requires version 2.0.
Results.Recommendation: Windows only shows this to administrators. Start the tool as administrator to include it: in the window use "Restart as administrator", in a console open PowerShell with "Run as administrator".

Results.Description: Full-disk encryption built into Windows. If the computer is lost or stolen, the data on the drive cannot be read without the key.
Results.Recommendation: Windows only shows this to administrators. Start the tool as administrator to include it: in the window use "Restart as administrator", in a console open PowerShell with "Run as administrator".

Results.Description: How often somebody tried to sign in with a wrong password. A few are mistyped passwords; many can mean someone is guessing passwords.
Results.Recommendation: Windows only shows this to administrators. Start the tool as administrator to include it: in the window use "Restart as administrator", in a console open PowerShell with "Run as administrator".

Results.Description: How often an account was locked because of too many wrong passwords.
Results.Recommendation: Windows only shows this to administrators. Start the tool as administrator to include it: in the window use "Restart as administrator", in a console open PowerShell with "Run as administrator".

Results.Description: A network card (cable or Wi-Fi) and its settings: the IP address identifies the computer, the gateway is the router, DNS servers translate names and DHCP hands all of this out automatically. Speed is the link speed the card negotiated.
How Windows classifies each connected network. Public hides the computer and uses the strictest firewall rules; Private is for a trusted home or office network; Domain is a company network.
A server that web traffic can be routed through. A wrong or leftover proxy setting stops browsers from reaching the internet.
A local list that maps names to IP addresses and is consulted before DNS. An entry there can redirect or block a web site on this computer only.
Shared folders on a server that appear as a drive letter. They are reconnected at every sign-in.
A test message sent to the router. A reply means the connection between the computer and the local network works.
A test message sent to a public server. A reply means traffic gets past the router and out to the internet.
DNS translates names such as microsoft.com into IP addresses. If it fails, web sites do not open even though the connection itself works.
A real web request over an encrypted connection. It confirms that the computer can actually reach web sites.
How far the clock of the computer is from internet time. A wrong clock causes certificate errors in the browser and failed sign-ins.
Results.Value: Differs from internet time by 1 second

Results.Description: The printer that programs use when no other one is chosen. Printing to the wrong printer is often just a wrong default.
The printers set up on this computer, including virtual ones such as "Microsoft Print to PDF".
Results.Value: 3 printers: Contoso LaserJet 400 (2nd floor), Microsoft Print to PDF, OneNote (Desktop)

Results.Description: The documents waiting to be printed. One stuck document blocks every document behind it.
DHCP Client asks the router for an IP address and network settings. If it is stopped, the computer cannot join a network automatically.
DNS Client translates names into IP addresses and remembers the answers. Without it web sites and network shares cannot be found by name.
Windows Event Log records what happens on the system. Many other services and all troubleshooting tools depend on it.
Workstation lets the computer connect to shared folders and printers on other computers.
Windows Defender Firewall filters network traffic and blocks unwanted incoming connections.
Microsoft Defender Antivirus Service protects the computer from malware. It is stopped when another antivirus is installed.
Windows Update finds, downloads and installs updates. It only runs when needed, so finding it stopped is normal.
Background Intelligent Transfer Service downloads updates in the background using idle bandwidth. It only runs when needed.
Print Spooler manages print jobs and sends them to the printers. If it is stopped, nothing can be printed.
Results.Recommendation: The service should start automatically but is not running. Start it in services.msc and check the System event log for the reason it stopped.
